[ASSISTANT_SAID] Sound design can enhance the narrative, mood, and tone of a film and provide a more immersive experience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Sound design can create a sense of place and time, establish character, and emotional connections with the audience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Specific sounds like footsteps, knocking, and creaking doors can generate suspense and tension in horror movies.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Sound design can create a sense of continuity in a film, helping the audience understand the overall structure and storyline.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Sound design conveys subliminal messages, such as emotions or themes, which the audience might not consciously process.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Overall, sound design captures the essence of the movie, enhancing the emotional experience and creating a more immersive cinematic environment.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of films with outstanding sound design include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. "Mad Max: Fury Road" (2015) - praised for its attention to detail, creating a gritty, post-apocalyptic atmosphere.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. "A Quiet Place" (2018) - sound design was a central element of the story, creating tension and fear with minimal dialogue.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. "Dunkirk" (2017) - sound design created urgency and chaos, with a ticking clock sound throughout to build tension.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Sound design is an essential element of the movie experience, impacting the story and message conveyed.
